title: Before All Things
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: God never needed us to complete his joy. Jesus was perfectly happy before all things, and he chose to come for us out of great love.
exhortation: This week we've seen Jesus as the image of the invisible God, the unapproachable God made known in human flesh. We've seen him as the firstborn of all creation, the heir and owner of all things, and as the one through whom everything in heaven and on earth was created. Now we see him before time itself: "He is before all things, and in him all things hold together."

Everything Jesus would later subject himself to in becoming a man, he existed before. What was there before everything we know? God, in all his fullness: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. There was never a time when he was not. And that was not some lonely existence. God wasn't bored or unhappy. Far from it. God in three persons existed in absolute happiness and joy. Imagine the fellowship of an endlessly creative being overflowing with joy. It breaks our brains.

Yet there's an idea that God somehow needed humanity to complete his joy or make heaven more full. At first that might seem to make God look kinder or more empathetic toward us, but in reality it cheapens his love. Jesus was before all things, and he was perfectly happy, in an unbroken happiness we can't wrap our minds around. Far from needing anything, he desired to create in his image.

And he, the Creator, was willing to take on a mysterious union with a mortal body. Attempts to explain away the deity of Christ, to suggest he was created or that there was a time when he was not, cheapen the unbelievable sacrifice he made. He didn't need to make it. He wanted to, because of the great love he has for us. What a Savior.
prayer: Lord, we stand in awe of you: the great I Am, outside of time, Creator of the universe, who needed nothing and yet showed your love for us by becoming a man and coming near to sinners. The one who had no sin became sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. It is astounding.

Open our eyes and soften our hearts to this truth today: though we had nothing and were helpless, those in Christ have everything they need and more, pressed down, shaken together and running over, because your love is unstoppable, unending and unchanging. Thank you, Lord.
